oil.summary: Crude surged sharply Tuesday as simultaneous supply shocks drove WTI to $89.59 (+4.44%) and Brent to $94.01 (+3.86%), with both benchmarks posting gains exceeding 11-12% on the month. The dominant catalyst is the active US-Iran military exchange: Iran has declared an oil blockade until attacks cease, a tanker was struck near Oman amid the Strait of Hormuz crisis, and Trump threatened further escalation. On the Russian front, Ukraine's drone barrage ignited the Ust-Luga Baltic export terminal, and prior strikes on refineries have forced Moscow to import jet fuel. The Washington administration partially eased Russia sanctions on a temporary basis to cool the price surge, drawing European pushback. RBOB gasoline was a stark outlier, collapsing 9.15% on the session — the data point stands alone with no headline explanation available today. Heating oil surged 3.59% and is up over 20% on the month, consistent with the distillate-tightening narrative.
drivers: US-Iran military conflict intensifying: Iran Hormuz blockade, tanker struck near Oman, Trump threatening further strikes
Ukrainian drone strike sets Russia's Ust-Luga oil export terminal ablaze, compounding earlier refinery damage that has cut Russian jet fuel supply
US temporarily eases Russia oil sanctions to cap the price surge; EU boards sixth suspected shadow-fleet tanker in parallel crackdown

gas.summary: European and Asian gas markets diverged sharply from a soft Henry Hub. TTF jumped 3.39% to €72.18/MWh, now up 25.5% on the month, driven by the ongoing Strait of Hormuz disruption: Asia spot LNG prices hit a five-month high as buyers scramble for spot cargoes with LNG traffic through the strait still constrained. Russia has responded to Western sanctions by doubling its dark-fleet LNG tanker count in nine months to sustain Arctic LNG 2 exports to Asia, further tightening spot availability for other buyers. Henry Hub slipped modestly to $2.898/MMBtu (-1.26%), suggesting domestic US fundamentals remain relatively comfortable, though the weekly gain of 4.62% hints at growing export-driven support. News flow on this sector is relatively limited beyond these three items.
drivers: Strait of Hormuz LNG disruption pushes Asia spot prices to a five-month high, lifting TTF by spillover demand competition
Russia doubles dark-fleet LNG vessel count to sustain sanctioned Arctic LNG 2 exports to Asia, tightening global spot supply
Henry Hub underperforms global benchmarks, slipping 1.26% on the day despite a 4.62% weekly gain, reflecting still-adequate domestic US supply

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs were broadly stable at $79.00 (+0.47%), lagging the sharp rally in TTF gas which underpins power-sector generation costs. Structural news was bullish for renewables: European wind capacity additions rose 30% year-on-year to 8.8 GW in H1 2026 per WindEurope data, while solar overtook coal as China's single largest installed electricity capacity source — a landmark in the global energy transition. US battery storage installations hit a record high in Q2, supporting grid reliability as intermittent capacity grows. On the risk side, Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant in Ukraine was reported to be relying on diesel generators after external power was cut, underscoring ongoing war-related infrastructure fragility. The muted EUA reaction to surging gas prices may reflect the offsetting effect of strong renewable additions on expected coal burn.
drivers: Solar surpasses coal as China's largest power capacity source; Europe wind additions up 30% in H1 — structural bearish pressure on carbon demand
US Q2 energy storage installations hit a record high, reinforcing grid decarbonisation momentum
Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant on diesel backup amid war tensions, highlighting acute European power infrastructure risk
